cobol_source:
*================================================================*
      * PROGRAM : CSVEXPRT                                             *
      * PURPOSE : CONVERT THE FIXED-WIDTH EMPLOYEE FILE TO CSV         *
      * INPUT   : data/input/employees.dat                             *
      * OUTPUT  : data/output/employees.csv                            *
      *================================================================*
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CSVEXPRT.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT EMP-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/input/employees.dat"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
           SELECT CSV-FILE ASSIGN TO "data/output/employees.csv"
               ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD  EMP-FILE.
           COPY EMPREC.
       FD  CSV-FILE.
       01  CSV-LINE                PIC X(100).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  WS-EOF                  PIC X VALUE 'N'.
           88  END-OF-FILE         VALUE 'Y'.
       01  WS-COUNT                PIC 9(03) VALUE 0.
       01  WS-SALARY-ED            PIC Z(06)9.99.
       01  WS-AGE-ED               PIC Z9.
       01  WS-PTR                  PIC 9(03).
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN-PARA.
           OPEN INPUT EMP-FILE OUTPUT CSV-FILE
           MOVE "id,name,department,salary,hire_date,age" TO CSV-LINE
           WRITE CSV-LINE
           PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE
               READ EMP-FILE
                   AT END SET END-OF-FILE TO TRUE
                   NOT AT END PERFORM WRITE-CSV
               END-READ
           END-PERFORM
           CLOSE EMP-FILE CSV-FILE
           DISPLAY "CSVEXPRT: " WS-COUNT " RECORDS EXPORTED"
           STOP RUN.
       WRITE-CSV.
           ADD 1 TO WS-COUNT
           MOVE EMP-SALARY TO WS-SALARY-ED
           MOVE EMP-AGE    TO WS-AGE-ED
           MOVE SPACES TO CSV-LINE
           MOVE 1 TO WS-PTR
           STRING EMP-ID                         DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-NAME)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(EMP-DEPT)        DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(WS-SALARY-ED)    DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  EMP-HIRE-YYYY "-" EMP-HIRE-MM "-" EMP-HIRE-DD
                                                 DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  ","                            DELIMITED BY SIZE
                  FUNCTION TRIM(WS-AGE-ED)       DELIMITED BY SIZE
               INTO CSV-LINE WITH POINTER WS-PTR
           END-STRING
           WRITE CSV-LINE.

plan.approach: The COBOL batch program reads a fixed-width flat file and writes a CSV. The modernised version replaces the flat-file I/O with a PostgreSQL table (employees) accessed through Spring Data JPA, retaining every formatting rule encoded in the COBOL PICTURE clauses and STRING statement. The program entry point (MAIN-PARA / STOP RUN) is exposed both as a REST endpoint (POST /api/v1/export/csv) and as an optional ApplicationRunner for pure batch execution controlled by a property flag.
patterns_used: Repository Pattern (Spring Data JPA EmployeeRepository replaces sequential READ loop)
Service Layer (CsvExportService encapsulates all PROCEDURE DIVISION logic)
REST Controller (CsvExportController exposes the export as an HTTP endpoint)
ApplicationRunner / Batch Mode (CsvExportRunner replicates STOP RUN batch behaviour)
Static Factory Methods (formatSalary, formatAge, formatHireDate mirror COBOL picture formatters)
Flyway Database Migration (V1 script creates the employees table matching the EMPREC copybook)
plan.sql_strategy: No EXEC SQL blocks existed in the original COBOL program (it read a flat file). The flat file (employees.dat) is replaced by a PostgreSQL employees table whose schema is derived from the EMPREC copybook fields. Spring Data JPA's findAll() replaces the PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE / READ loop, streaming all rows into the CSV formatting pipeline.
plan.call_strategy: No CALL statements existed in the original program. The COBOL intrinsic function FUNCTION TRIM is replaced by Java String.trim(). The PICTURE clause numeric editors (Z(06)9.99 and Z9) are implemented as static helper methods (formatSalary, formatAge, applyZeroSuppression) that faithfully reproduce COBOL zero-suppression and decimal formatting rules. The COBOL STRING verb with POINTER is replicated using a StringBuilder append chain.
